items.actClause: AN ACT authorizing a certain housing authority to sell or lease all or part of certain housing developments

A.actClause: AN ACT authorizing a certain housing authority to transfer or restructure the ownership of all or part of certain housing developments
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A9487A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act authorizing a certain housing authority to trans-
fer or restructure the ownership of all or part of certain housing
developments

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:  This legislation would make these
developments eligible for federal support.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:  The bill authorizes the New York City
Housing Authority to sell or lease all or part of the projects commonly
known as Marlboro Houses, Chelsea Houses, Castle Hill Houses, 344 East
28th Street, Amsterdam Addition, Bushwick Houses, Stephen Wise Towers,
Arthur H. Murphy Houses, Baychester Houses, Jonathan Williams Plaza,
Drew-Hamilton Houses, Independence Towers, Rutgers Houses, Stapleton
Houses and Manhattanville Houses, located in the city of New York, coun-
ties of Bronx, Kings, New York and Richmond, for the purpose of rehabil-
itation of the projects.

In particular, section 1 sets out the legislative findings. Section 2
authorizes the New York City Housing Authority, with the approval of the
commissioner of housing and community renewal, to sell all or part of
the part of the projects commonly known as Marlboro Houses, Chelsea
Houses, Castle Hill Houses, 344 East 28th Street, Amsterdam Addition,
Bushwick Houses, Stephen Wise Towers, Arthur H. Murphy Houses, Bayches-
ter Houses, Jonathan Williams Plaza, Drew-Hamilton Houses, Independence
Towers, Rutgers Houses, Stapleton Houses and Manhattanville Houses in
the city of New York for the purpose of rehabilitating the project for
low income families. Section 3 establishes the guidelines for occupancy
to ensure that the units remain public housing and that all laws rules
and regulations applicable to federal public housing projects continue
to apply after the sale or lease of the project. Section 4 continues
state subsidies for debt service on outstanding bonds, notes or other
obligations.  Section 5 is the effective date which provides that the
act shall take immediately, provided, however, that the provisions of
section 4 of this act shall apply to any debt service payments which
become due after such date.

JUSTIFICATION:  Currently, none of these developments are included in
the formulas by which HUD provides NYCHA Operating and Capital subsi-
dies. As a result, NYCHA must draw down from its regular Federal Operat-
ing fund and Capital fund and apply them to the State and City develop-
ments.  This lack of dedicated Federal subsidy, and the elimination of
State operating subsidies, has contributed to operating deficits at not
just the State/City developments, but to the structural deficits NYCHA
is experiencing on agency-wide bases.

The American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA) provides NYCHA with a
one-time opportunity to address the deficits generated at the State/City
developments and to ameliorate NYCHA's structural deficit.  ARRA permits
public housing authorities to bring additional units into the federal
public housing portfolio and receive full Federal funding so long as

such units are developed using ARRA. funding.  Since the physical needs
of the State developments are so significant, non-Federal funds in addi-
tion to ARRA funds will be required to undertake and complete the level
of necessary rehabilitation. In order to accomplish this, NYCHA will be
required to employ HUD's mixed-finance approach for public housing
developments, but must do so within the strict obligation and expendi-
ture deadlines imposed by ARRA, on or no later than March 17, 2010.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to the State

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately, provided,
however, that the provisions of section four of this act shall apply to
any debt service payments which become due after such date.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the public housing law, in relation to authorizing the New York city housing authority to enter into mixed-finance transactions in order to preserve the continued availability of low-income housing to public housing residents of the city of New York
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:A9487B

TITLE  OF BILL:   An act to amend the public housing law, in relation to
authorizing the New York city housing authority to enter into  mixed-fi-
nance  transactions  in  order to preserve the continued availability of
low-income housing to public housing residents of the city of New York

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:  This legislation is necessary in order
for these developments to become eligible for federal support.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:  The bill authorizes the New  York  City
Housing  Authority  (NYCHA) to sell or lease all or part of the projects
commonly known as Marlboro Houses, Chelsea Houses,- Castle Hill  Houses,
344  East 28th Street, Amsterdam Addition, Bushwick Houses, Stephen Wise
Towers, Arthur H.  Murphy Houses, Baychester Houses,  Jonathan  Williams
Plaza,   Drew-Hamilton  Houses,  Independence  Towers,  Rutgers  Houses,
Stapleton Houses and Manhattanville Houses, located in the city  of  New
York,  counties  of Bronx, Kings, New York and Richmond, for the purpose
of rehabilitation of the projects.

In particular, subdivision 1 sets out the legislative findings.  Enumer-
ated in this subdivision are protections for tenants  in  city  financed
Projects.  The  city  financed  projects include Marble Hill Houses, St.
Mary's Park Houses, Bay View Houses, Boulevard  Houses,  Linden  Houses,
and  Samuel  Houses.  Subdivision 2 authorizes the New York City Housing
Authority, with the approval of the  commissioner  of  the  division  of
housing  and  community  renewal,  to  sell  or lease all or part of the
projects commonly known as Marlboro Houses, Chelsea Houses, Castle  Hill
Houses,  344  East  28th  Street,  Amsterdam  Addition, Bushwick Houses,
Stephen Wise Towers, Arthur H. Murphy Houses, Baychester  Houses,  Jona-
than  Williams Plaza, Drew-Hamilton Houses, Independence Towers, Rutgers
Houses, Stapleton Houses, and Manhattanville Houses in the city  of  New
York  for  the  purpose of redeveloping the project for low income fami-
lies. The commissioner shall  not  grant  approval  unless  new  federal
assistance  is significantly more likely to be available after rehabili-
tation and new operation. Subdivision 3 establishes the  guidelines  for
occupancy,  and that all applicable requirements of federal public hous-
ing projects continue to apply after the sale or lease of  the  project.
Subdivision  4 continues state subsidies for debt service on outstanding
bonds, notes, or other  obligations  for  the  projects.  Subdivision  5
requires  the  New  York City Housing Authority to circulate a notice to
all tenants in the listed public housing projects,  containing  informa-
tion  regarding  the transfer and federalization process, as well as the
tenants' rights. Subdivision 6 requires copies  of  the  annual  project
activity  report,  which  is related to both the state and city projects
listed in this section, to be submitted to the commissioner of the divi-
sion of housing and community Renewal and to various  elected  officials
in the Assembly and the Senate.

Section  2  states that the act shall take effect immediately, provided,
however; that the provisions of subdivision 4 of section  402-b  of  the

public housing law shall apply to any debt service payments which become
due after such date.

JUSTIFICATION:    Currently,  none of these developments are included in
the formulas by which HUD provides NYCHA Operating  and  Capital  subsi-
dies. As a result, NYCHA must draw down from its regular Federal Operat-
ing  fund and Capital fund and apply them to the State and City develop-
ments.  This lack of dedicated Federal subsidy, and the  elimination  of
State  operating subsidies, has contributed to operating deficits at not
just the State/City developments, but to the structural  deficits  NYCHA
is experiencing on agency-wide bases.

The  American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (ARRA) provides NYCHA with a
one-time opportunity to address the deficits generated at the State/City
developments and to ameliorate NYCHA's structural deficit.  ARRA permits
Public housing authorities to bring additional units  into  the  federal
public  housing  portfolio  and  receive full Federal funding so long as
such units are developed using ARRA funding. Since the physical needs of
the State developments are so significant, non-Federal funds in addition
to ARRA funds will be required to undertake and complete  the  level  of
necessary  rehabilitation.  In  order  to accomplish this, NYCHA will be
required to employ  HUD's  mixed-finance  approach  for  public  housing
developments,  but  must do so within the strict obligation and expendi-
ture deadlines imposed by ARRA, on or no later than March 17,  2010.  Be
receiving operating and capital subsidies from the federal government on
a  regular  basis,  it ensures that the state and city financed projects
will remain public housing within  the  financial  reach  of  low-income
persons or families.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New Bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to the State

EFFECTIVE DATE: This act shall take effect immediately, provided, howev-
er,  that  the provisions of section four of this act shall apply to any
debt service payments which become due after such date.

summary: Authorizes the NYC housing authority to transfer or restructure the ownership of all or part of certain housing developments.
